- Avoid over-optimism in early forecast periods; model tends to overestimate prices in the first 5–7 days after a spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00), model should not assume momentum; price corrections are more likely than continuation.
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a forecast decline, it often overcorrects — reduce the magnitude of the subsequent drop.
- Mean reversion is stronger in the 10–15 day horizon; model often underestimates pullback after a 30-day peak.
- Forecasting 30-day ahead should not ignore recent 18-day history — model frequently ignores recent lows and overweights distant trends.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–3% to avoid “overshoot after spike” bias.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model should not assume volatility — price may remain stable or revert to mean, not trend.
- Model tends to underestimate late-period (last 5–7 days) true values — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for final 7–10 days of horizon.
